evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: The structural diagnostics describe the current two-set partition in the fused patient geometry. Both candidate sets have similar sizes (55 and 48) and nearly equal mean within-set affinities (about 0.00929 and 0.00936), indicating comparable internal cohesion. The mean between-set affinity (about 0.00902) is only marginally lower than the within-set values, so the current boundary between K2_C0001 and K2_C0002 is not strongly separated in this fused affinity representation. Within each set, the eigengap profile is dominated by the leading gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k = 1 for both sets), with subsequent gaps orders of magnitude smaller. This means the screening calculation does not identify a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal and does not supply feasible k>=2 internal solutions; it should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Overall, the measurements indicate that the two current sets are internally cohesive to a similar degree and that their mutual boundary is relatively weak in fused affinity terms, while the internal screening results are dominated by the single-cluster resolution rather than by any feasible internal split.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 (55 patients versus 48 rest), the RNA pathway enrichment is estimable and yields a coherent, multi-program phenotype. The dominant up-regulated signal is oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.29, FDR 0.001), with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle genes, accompanied by up-regulation of reactive-oxygen-species response (NES 1.82), fatty-acid metabolism, and adipogenesis. A second coherent axis is immune/inflammatory: interferon-gamma and interferon-alpha responses, allograft rejection, IL6/JAK/STAT3, complement, inflammatory response, and apoptosis are all up-regulated with FDRs between 0.0015 and 0.040, and their leading edges share HLA, STAT1, IRF1, CXCL9/10/11, and cytotoxic T-cell genes. A third axis is proliferative: DNA repair, E2F targets, G2/M checkpoint, MYC targets, mTORC1 signaling, and glycolysis are up-regulated, with leading edges including PCNA, MKI67, TOP2A, CDK1, and PLK1. Down-regulated programs include UV response DN (NES -1.87, FDR 0.0065), TGF-beta signaling, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, with leading edges including PTEN, TGFBR2, SMAD6/7, and NOTCH1. The pattern is internally consistent: a metabolically active, immune-infiltrated, proliferative phenotype with reduced TGF-beta/Wnt/Hedgehog signaling. Because this is a K=2 set-versus-rest contrast, the reciprocal K2_C0002 report is the same two-group contrast viewed from the other side, not an independent confirmation. The FDR values indicate pathway-level multiplicity control, but the magnitude and coherence of the leading-edge gene sets, not the FDR alone, are what make the phenotype interpretable.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The only prior Evidence Report is the structural diagnostics for the partition. That report found the two sets to be internally cohesive to a similar degree and the between-set boundary relatively weak in fused affinity terms, with eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. The RNA enrichment here provides a biological characterization of K2_C0001 that is complementary to that structural picture: it describes a distinct metabolic/immune/proliferative program relative to the rest, but it does not resolve the weak structural boundary noted in the prior report. The two reports address different dimensions and do not conflict; the structural report does not speak to pathway biology, and this report does not speak to geometry.
limitations: The enrichment is a set-versus-rest contrast in a K=2 partition; the reciprocal K2_C0002 report is the same contrast from the other side and is not an independent biological confirmation.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002 (48 patients versus 55 rest), the RNA pathway enrichment is estimable and is the exact reciprocal of the K2_C0001 contrast. The dominant down-regulated program is oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.29, FDR 0.001), with the same mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle leading edge that is up-regulated in K2_C0001. Immune/inflammatory programs are down-regulated: allograft rejection, interferon-gamma and interferon-alpha responses, complement, and IL6/JAK/STAT3 signaling all have negative NES and FDRs between 0.0018 and 0.0052, with leading edges including HLA, STAT1, IRF1, CXCL9/10/11, and cytotoxic T-cell genes. Proliferative programs are also down-regulated: DNA repair, E2F targets, MYC targets V1/V2, G2/M checkpoint, glycolysis, and mTORC1 signaling, with leading edges including PCNA, MKI67, TOP2A, CDK1, and PLK1. Up-regulated programs include UV response DN (NES 1.84, FDR 0.0063), TGF-beta signaling, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, with leading edges including PTEN, TGFBR2, SMAD6/7, and NOTCH1. This is the mirror image of the K2_C0001 profile: K2_C0002 is characterized by lower oxidative phosphorylation, lower immune/inflammatory infiltration, lower proliferation, and relatively higher TGF-beta/Wnt/Hedgehog signaling. Because the two K=2 contrasts are reciprocal views of the same two-group comparison, this report does not independently confirm the K2_C0001 phenotype; it describes the opposite side of the same contrast.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 versus rest, several measured technical and acquisition factors show statistically significant association after BH correction: tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.434, q 0.009), CT phase (V 0.316, q 0.028), CT scanner model (V 0.310, q 0.028), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.066, q 0.026), and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.048, q 0.028). CT manufacturer, reconstruction kernel, pixel spacing, and study year are not significant after correction. The strongest categorical association is tissue source site, with K2_C0001 enriched for BP and depleted for CJ and CZ relative to rest; CT phase and scanner model also show imbalance, with K2_C0001 having more UNKNOWN phase and more Sensation 64 and LightSpeed16 scanners. These associations indicate that the candidate membership is not independent of site and acquisition characteristics, and the effect sizes for tissue source site, CT phase, and scanner model are moderate. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors could reflect real biological differences that happen to correlate with site or acquisition, or they could contribute to the geometry. The continuous factors show small effect sizes (epsilon-squared 0.048-0.066), so their practical contribution is limited even where significant. The nonsignificant factors (manufacturer, kernel, pixel spacing, study year) do not establish absence of confounding, and the analysis covers only the measured factors.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural diagnostics report found the between-set boundary relatively weak in fused affinity terms and the two sets internally cohesive to a similar degree. The confounder associations here are relevant to that structural picture because tissue source site and CT acquisition factors are associated with K2_C0001 membership, which could contribute to the fused geometry. However, the structural report did not include technical-factor analyses, and this report does not include geometry, so the two are complementary rather than conflicting. The RNA enrichment reports describe a biological phenotype for K2_C0001; the confounder associations here do not contradict that phenotype but raise the possibility that some of the signal is confounded by site or acquisition.
limitations: Association is not causation; significant factors may reflect real biology correlated with site or acquisition rather than technical artifact.
Nonsignificant factors do not establish absence of confounding.
The analysis covers only the measured factors; unmeasured technical or biological confounders are not assessed.
The contingency tables have many sparse cells (e.g., G6, CJ, CZ), which can make chi-square and Cramer's V unstable.
The continuous-factor tests use Kruskal-Wallis, which assesses distributional differences and does not separate location from dispersion.

The strongest categorical association is tissue source site, with K2_C0001 enriched for BP and depleted for CJ and CZ relative to rest; CT phase and scanner model also show imbalance, with K2_C0001 having more UNKNOWN phase and more Sensation 64 and LightSpeed16 scanners. These associations indicate that the candidate membership is not independent of site and acquisition characteristics, and the effect sizes for tissue source site, CT phase, and scanner model are moderate. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors could reflect real biological differences that happen to correlate with site or acquisition, or they could contribute to the geometry. The continuous factors show small effect sizes (epsilon-squared 0.048-0.066), so their practical contribution is limited even where significant. The nonsignificant factors (manufacturer, kernel, pixel spacing, study year) do not establish absence of confounding, and the analysis covers only the measured factors.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 (55 patients versus 48 rest), the WXS mutation enrichment is estimable and yields a coherent, interpretable driver-level phenotype. The dominant signal is a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 pattern: VHL is strongly depleted in K2_C0001 (18/55 vs 38/48; OR 0.128, q_driver 5.2e-05, q_global 0.012) and PBRM1 is depleted (14/55 vs 25/48; OR 0.314, q_driver 0.040), while BAP1 is strongly enriched (13/55 vs 0/48; OR 30.8 with a 0.5 Haldane-Anscombe correction, q_driver 0.0012). This is a recognizable ccRCC mutational axis in which BAP1-mutant tumors tend to be VHL/PBRM1-wild-type. The driver-family and global multiplicity questions diverge: VHL is significant under both q_driver and q_global, whereas BAP1 and PBRM1 are significant only within the prespecified driver family (q_global 0.275 and 1.0, respectively), so their global-family evidence is weaker. The remaining driver genes (MTOR, TP53, KDM5C, SETD2, and others) show no significant enrichment or depletion, and CDKN2A has no events in either group, so no effect is estimable. The exploratory non-driver genes show only nominal associations that do not survive global correction. Overall, the mutation data describe a driver-level phenotype centered on the VHL/PBRM1/BAP1 axis, with the caveat that only VHL is significant across the full tested-gene family.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior reports for this partition include structural diagnostics (weak between-set boundary in fused affinity, comparable internal cohesion, eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution), RNA pathway enrichment for both sets (K2_C0001 up in oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs; K2_C0002 the reciprocal), and confounder associations (tissue source site and CT acquisition factors significantly associated with membership). The WXS driver pattern here is complementary to the RNA phenotype: the BAP1-enriched, VHL/PBRM1-depleted mutational profile of K2_C0001 is a distinct biological axis from the RNA programs, and the two modalities address different molecular layers rather than confirming each other. The confounder report raises the possibility that site or acquisition contributes to the geometry, but it does not speak to mutation biology, so there is no direct conflict; the mutation findings neither resolve nor are resolved by the weak structural boundary.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: The structural diagnostics describe the current two-set partition in the fused patient geometry. Both candidate sets are moderately sized and roughly balanced (55 and 48), and their mean within-set affinities are essentially identical (about 0.00932 for both), indicating comparable internal cohesion. The mean between-set affinity (about 0.00902) is only marginally lower than the within-set values, and the boundary silhouette is near zero (0.0003), so the current boundary between K2_C0001 and K2_C0002 is not sharply separated in this fused affinity representation. evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: This report addresses whether the current K2_C0001/K2_C0002 memberships, internal structures, and boundary are coherently represented across the four native patient geometries. The current-label alignment is weak in every single view: the boundary silhouette is near zero in CT (0.013) and small in WSI (0.050), RNA (0.079), and WXS (0.091), and in each modality the mean between-label distance exceeds the mean within-label distance only marginally. This means the current pair boundary is directionally present but not sharply expressed in any one modality's native distance geometry, and the tool performs no reclustering, so these values describe alignment of the existing labels rather than a re-derived partition. The GRV results describe a separate question: global similarity between modality patient geometries. GRV is modest for all six modality pairs (0.092-0.198), with the highest values for WSI-RNA and CT-WSI and the lowest for CT-WXS and WSI-WXS. Permutation evidence indicates that patient correspondence is unlikely under exchangeability for CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA (p = 0.001), is marginal for CT-RNA and WSI-WXS, and is not distinguishable from exchangeable for CT-WXS. Bootstrap intervals for all GRVs exclude zero and are fairly narrow, so the modest positive similarity is stable under paired patient resampling, though the intervals overlap across pairs. Importantly, high GRV would not by itself establish that two views support the same candidate boundary, and the modest GRVs here coexist with weak current-label alignment in every view; low GRV (e.g., CT-WXS) can reflect complementary rather than faulty information. Taken together, the measurements indicate that the four views share only modest global patient-geometry structure and that none of them sharply separates the current K2 boundary, so the current memberships are not strongly reinforced by cross-view geometric concordance.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior reports for this partition include structural diagnostics on the fused geometry (comparable internal cohesion, near-zero boundary silhouette, eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution), RNA pathway enrichment for both sets (K2_C0001 up in oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs; K2_C0002 the reciprocal), confounder associations (tissue source site and CT acquisition factors significantly associated with membership), and WXS mutation enrichment (a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 driver axis). The present concordance report is complementary to the fused-geometry structural report: both indicate a weak current boundary, but this report shows that weakness holds in each modality's native geometry individually, not only in the fused representation, and it adds that global patient-geometry similarity across views is modest. The confounder report is the most relevant tension, since significant site and acquisition associations could contribute to the CT and fused geometries in which alignment is weakest; however, association is not proof of artifact, and this concordance analysis cannot adjudicate that question. The RNA and WXS reports describe coherent set-level biology that is not in direct conflict with the geometric picture, but this report does not validate those biological findings, and the modest GRVs do not constitute independent confirmation of the candidate boundary.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 (55 patients versus 48 rest), the RNA pathway enrichment is estimable and yields a coherent, multi-program phenotype. The dominant up-regulated signal is oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.29, FDR 0.001), with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle genes, accompanied by up-regulation of reactive-oxygen-species response (NES 1.82), fatty-acid metabolism, and adipogenesis. A second coherent axis is immune/inflammatory: interferon-gamma and interferon-alpha responses, allograft rejection, IL6/JAK/STAT3, complement, inflammatory response, and apoptosis are all up-regulated with FDRs between 0.0015 and 0.040, and their leading edges share HLA, STAT1, IRF1, CXCL9/10/11, and cytotoxic T-cell genes. A third axis is proliferative: DNA repair, E2F targets, G2/M checkpoint, MYC targets, mTORC1 signaling, and glycolysis are up-regulated, with leading edges including PCNA, MKI67, TOP2A, CDK1, and PLK1. Down-regulated programs include UV response DN (NES -1.87, FDR 0.0065), TGF-beta signaling, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, with leading edges including PTEN, TGFBR2, SMAD6/7, and NOTCH1. The pattern is internally consistent: a metabolically active, immune-infiltrated, proliferative phenotype with reduced TGF-beta/Wnt/Hedgehog signaling. Because this is a K=2 set-versus-rest contrast, the reciprocal K2_C0002 report is the same two-group contrast viewed from the other side, not an independent confirmation. The FDR values indicate pathway-level multiplicity control, but the magnitude and coherence of the leading-edge gene sets, not the FDR alone, are what make the phenotype interpretable.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The only prior Evidence Report is the structural diagnostics for the partition. That report found the two sets to be internally cohesive to a similar degree and the between-set boundary relatively weak in fused affinity terms, with eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. The RNA enrichment here provides a biological characterization of K2_C0001 that is complementary to that structural picture: it describes a distinct metabolic/immune/proliferative program relative to the rest, but it does not resolve the weak structural boundary noted in the prior report. The two reports address different dimensions and do not conflict; the structural report does not speak to pathway biology, and this report does not speak to geometry.
limitations: The enrichment is a set-versus-rest contrast in a K=2 partition; the reciprocal K2_C0002 report is the same contrast from the other side and is not an independent biological confirmation.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 versus rest, several measured technical and acquisition factors show statistically significant association after BH correction: tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.434, q 0.009), CT phase (V 0.316, q 0.028), CT scanner model (V 0.310, q 0.028), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.066, q 0.026), and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.048, q 0.028). CT manufacturer, reconstruction kernel, pixel spacing, and study year are not significant after correction. The strongest categorical association is tissue source site, with K2_C0001 enriched for BP and depleted for CJ and CZ relative to rest; CT phase and scanner model also show imbalance, with K2_C0001 having more UNKNOWN phase and more Sensation 64 and LightSpeed16 scanners. These associations indicate that the candidate membership is not independent of site and acquisition characteristics, and the effect sizes for tissue source site, CT phase, and scanner model are moderate. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors could reflect real biological differences that happen to correlate with site or acquisition, or they could contribute to the geometry. The continuous factors show small effect sizes (epsilon-squared 0.048-0.066), so their practical contribution is limited even where significant. The nonsignificant factors (manufacturer, kernel, pixel spacing, study year) do not establish absence of confounding, and the analysis covers only the measured factors.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 (55 patients versus 48 rest), the WXS mutation enrichment is estimable and yields a coherent, interpretable driver-level phenotype. The dominant signal is a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 pattern: VHL is strongly depleted in K2_C0001 (18/55 vs 38/48; OR 0.128, q_driver 5.2e-05, q_global 0.012) and PBRM1 is depleted (14/55 vs 25/48; OR 0.314, q_driver 0.040), while BAP1 is strongly enriched (13/55 vs 0/48; OR 30.8 with a 0.5 Haldane-Anscombe correction, q_driver 0.0012). This is a recognizable ccRCC mutational axis in which BAP1-mutant tumors tend to be VHL/PBRM1-wild-type. The driver-family and global multiplicity questions diverge: VHL is significant under both q_driver and q_global, whereas BAP1 and PBRM1 are significant only within the prespecified driver family (q_global 0.275 and 1.0, respectively), so their global-family evidence is weaker. The remaining driver genes (MTOR, TP53, KDM5C, SETD2, and others) show no significant enrichment or depletion, and CDKN2A has no events in either group, so no effect is estimable. The exploratory non-driver genes show only nominal associations that do not survive global correction. Overall, the mutation data describe a driver-level phenotype centered on the VHL/PBRM1/BAP1 axis, with the caveat that only VHL is significant across the full tested-gene family.

The confounder report raises the possibility that site or acquisition contributes to the geometry, but it does not speak to mutation biology, so there is no direct conflict; the mutation findings neither resolve nor are resolved by the weak structural boundary.

This is the mirror image of the K2_C0001 profile and describes the same VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 mutational axis from the opposite side. As in K2_C0001, only VHL is significant under global BH correction, while BAP1 and PBRM1 are significant only within the prespecified driver family (q_global 0.275 and 1.0). The remaining driver genes show no significant enrichment or depletion, and CDKN2A has no events in either group. The exploratory non-driver genes show only nominal associations that do not survive global correction. Because the K=2 contrasts are reciprocal, this report does not independently confirm the K2_C0001 mutation findings; it describes the same two-group comparison from the other side.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior reports for this partition include structural diagnostics (weak between-set boundary in fused affinity, comparable internal cohesion, eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution), RNA pathway enrichment for both sets (K2_C0002 down in oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs relative to K2_C0001), and confounder associations (tissue source site and CT acquisition factors significantly associated with membership). The WXS driver pattern here is the reciprocal of the K2_C0001 mutation report and is complementary to the RNA phenotype: the VHL/PBRM1-enriched, BAP1-depleted profile of K2_C0002 is a distinct molecular layer from the RNA programs. The confounder report raises the possibility that site or acquisition contributes to the geometry but does not speak to mutation biology, so there is no direct conflict. The mutation findings neither resolve nor are resolved by the weak structural boundary.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: This report addresses whether the current K2_C0001/K2_C0002 memberships, internal structures, and boundary are coherently represented across the four native patient geometries. The current-label alignment is weak in every single view: the boundary silhouette is near zero in CT (0.013) and small in WSI (0.050), RNA (0.079), and WXS (0.091), and in each modality the mean between-label distance exceeds the mean within-label distance only marginally. This means the current pair boundary is directionally present but not sharply expressed in any one modality's native distance geometry, and the tool performs no reclustering, so these values describe alignment of the existing labels rather than a re-derived partition. The GRV results describe a separate question: global similarity between modality patient geometries. GRV is modest for all six modality pairs (0.092-0.198), with the highest values for WSI-RNA and CT-WSI and the lowest for CT-WXS and WSI-WXS. Permutation evidence indicates that patient correspondence is unlikely under exchangeability for CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA (p = 0.001), is marginal for CT-RNA and WSI-WXS, and is not distinguishable from exchangeable for CT-WXS. Bootstrap intervals for all GRVs exclude zero and are fairly narrow, so the modest positive similarity is stable under paired patient resampling, though the intervals overlap across pairs. Importantly, high GRV would not by itself establish that two views support the same candidate boundary, and the modest GRVs here coexist with weak current-label alignment in every view; low GRV (e.g., CT-WXS) can reflect complementary rather than faulty information. Taken together, the measurements indicate that the four views share only modest global patient-geometry structure and that none of them sharply separates the current K2 boundary, so the current memberships are not strongly reinforced by cross-view geometric concordance.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior reports for this partition include structural diagnostics on the fused geometry (comparable internal cohesion, near-zero boundary silhouette, eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution), RNA pathway enrichment for both sets (K2_C0001 up in oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs; K2_C0002 the reciprocal), confounder associations (tissue source site and CT acquisition factors significantly associated with membership), and WXS mutation enrichment (a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 driver axis). The present concordance report is complementary to the fused-geometry structural report: both indicate a weak current boundary, but this report shows that weakness holds in each modality's native geometry individually, not only in the fused representation, and it adds that global patient-geometry similarity across views is modest. The confounder report is the most relevant tension, since significant site and acquisition associations could contribute to the CT and fused geometries in which alignment is weakest; however, association is not proof of artifact, and this concordance analysis cannot adjudicate that question. The RNA and WXS reports describe coherent set-level biology that is not in direct conflict with the geometric picture, but this report does not validate those biological findings, and the modest GRVs do not constitute independent confirmation of the candidate boundary.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: The partition shows weak-to-moderate, nominally significant associations with several clinical stratification variables. Grade, overall stage, T stage, and M stage all have Cramer's V in the 0.20-0.27 range with p-values between 0.018 and 0.032, and the direction is consistent across them: K2_C0001 carries proportionally more high-grade (G4), advanced-stage (III/IV), higher T stage (T3/T4), and M1 disease, while K2_C0002 is enriched for lower-stage (I) and lower T stage (T1) disease. The effect sizes are modest, so the partition is not a clean recapitulation of any single clinical variable, and the clinical labels are not independent of the partition but also not strongly aligned with it. For the established expression-derived taxonomies, correspondence is modest to weak: ClearCode34 shows ARI 0.240 and AMI 0.181 with K2_C0001 leaning ccB and K2_C0002 leaning ccA, while TCGA m1-m4 shows ARI 0.146 and AMI 0.133 with K2_C0002 concentrated in m1. Because both taxonomies are derived from expression and overlap the RNA discovery view, these values describe correspondence within the same data domain rather than external validation, and the chance-adjusted agreement is low enough that the partition is not simply reproducing either taxonomy. Coverage differs across comparisons (103 for clinical variables, 98 for M stage, 76 for ClearCode34, 84 for TCGA m1-m4), so the taxonomy comparisons rest on smaller reference sets than the clinical ones.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior reports for this partition describe a weak fused-geometry boundary with comparable internal cohesion and eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution; coherent reciprocal RNA programs (oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs higher in K2_C0001); a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 WXS driver axis; significant tissue source site and CT acquisition associations; and modest cross-view geometry concordance with weak current-label alignment in every modality. The clinical associations here are consistent with the RNA and WXS biological characterization in direction: K2_C0001, which is enriched for oxidative-phosphorylation/immune/proliferative programs and BAP1 mutation with VHL/PBRM1 depletion, is also the set carrying more high-grade, advanced-stage, and M1 disease. This is complementarity across dimensions rather than independent confirmation, since the clinical variables are not a separate molecular assay and the taxonomy comparisons overlap the RNA discovery view. The modest ClearCode34 and TCGA m1-m4 correspondence does not resolve the weak structural boundary noted in the geometry reports, and the significant site/acquisition associations remain a tension that the clinical-label results neither confirm nor refute.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 (55 patients versus 48 rest), the RNA pathway enrichment is estimable and yields a coherent, multi-program phenotype. The dominant up-regulated signal is oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.29, FDR 0.001), with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle genes, accompanied by up-regulation of reactive-oxygen-species response (NES 1.82), fatty-acid metabolism, and adipogenesis. A second coherent axis is immune/inflammatory: interferon-gamma and interferon-alpha responses, allograft rejection, IL6/JAK/STAT3, complement, inflammatory response, and apoptosis are all up-regulated with FDRs between 0.0015 and 0.040, and their leading edges share HLA, STAT1, IRF1, CXCL9/10/11, and cytotoxic T-cell genes. A third axis is proliferative: DNA repair, E2F targets, G2/M checkpoint, MYC targets, mTORC1 signaling, and glycolysis are up-regulated, with leading edges including PCNA, MKI67, TOP2A, CDK1, and PLK1. Down-regulated programs include UV response DN (NES -1.87, FDR 0.0065), TGF-beta signaling, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, with leading edges including PTEN, TGFBR2, SMAD6/7, and NOTCH1. The pattern is internally consistent: a metabolically active, immune-infiltrated, proliferative phenotype with reduced TGF-beta/Wnt/Hedgehog signaling. Because this is a K=2 set-versus-rest contrast, the reciprocal K2_C0002 report is the same two-group contrast viewed from the other side, not an independent confirmation. The FDR values indicate pathway-level multiplicity control, but the magnitude and coherence of the leading-edge gene sets, not the FDR alone, are what make the phenotype interpretable.

The two reports address different dimensions and do not conflict; the structural report does not speak to pathway biology, and this report does not speak to geometry.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002 (48 patients versus 55 rest), the RNA pathway enrichment is estimable and is the exact reciprocal of the K2_C0001 contrast. The dominant down-regulated program is oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.29, FDR 0.001), with the same mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle leading edge that is up-regulated in K2_C0001. Immune/inflammatory programs are down-regulated: allograft rejection, interferon-gamma and interferon-alpha responses, complement, and IL6/JAK/STAT3 signaling all have negative NES and FDRs between 0.0018 and 0.0052, with leading edges including HLA, STAT1, IRF1, CXCL9/10/11, and cytotoxic T-cell genes. Proliferative programs are also down-regulated: DNA repair, E2F targets, MYC targets V1/V2, G2/M checkpoint, glycolysis, and mTORC1 signaling, with leading edges including PCNA, MKI67, TOP2A, CDK1, and PLK1. Up-regulated programs include UV response DN (NES 1.84, FDR 0.0063), TGF-beta signaling, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, with leading edges including PTEN, TGFBR2, SMAD6/7, and NOTCH1. This is the mirror image of the K2_C0001 profile: K2_C0002 is characterized by lower oxidative phosphorylation, lower immune/inflammatory infiltration, lower proliferation, and relatively higher TGF-beta/Wnt/Hedgehog signaling. Because the two K=2 contrasts are reciprocal views of the same two-group comparison, this report does not independently confirm the K2_C0001 phenotype; it describes the opposite side of the same contrast.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The only prior Evidence Report is the structural diagnostics for the partition, which found the two sets internally cohesive to a similar degree and the between-set boundary relatively weak in fused affinity terms, with eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. The RNA enrichment here provides a biological characterization of K2_C0002 that is complementary to that structural picture and is the reciprocal of the K2_C0001 enrichment report. The two RNA reports together describe a coherent biological axis (oxidative phosphorylation, immune infiltration, and proliferation higher in K2_C0001 and lower in K2_C0002), but they are not independent confirmations of each other. The structural report does not speak to pathway biology, and this report does not speak to geometry.
limitations: The enrichment is a set-versus-rest contrast in a K=2 partition; the K2_C0001 report is the same contrast from the other side and is not an independent biological confirmation.

The continuous factors show small effect sizes (epsilon-squared 0.048-0.066), so their practical contribution is limited even where significant. The nonsignificant factors (manufacturer, kernel, pixel spacing, study year) do not establish absence of confounding, and the analysis covers only the measured factors.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 (55 patients versus 48 rest), the WXS mutation enrichment is estimable and yields a coherent, interpretable driver-level phenotype. The dominant signal is a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 pattern: VHL is strongly depleted in K2_C0001 (18/55 vs 38/48; OR 0.128, q_driver 5.2e-05, q_global 0.012) and PBRM1 is depleted (14/55 vs 25/48; OR 0.314, q_driver 0.040), while BAP1 is strongly enriched (13/55 vs 0/48; OR 30.8 with a 0.5 Haldane-Anscombe correction, q_driver 0.0012). This is a recognizable ccRCC mutational axis in which BAP1-mutant tumors tend to be VHL/PBRM1-wild-type. The driver-family and global multiplicity questions diverge: VHL is significant under both q_driver and q_global, whereas BAP1 and PBRM1 are significant only within the prespecified driver family (q_global 0.275 and 1.0, respectively), so their global-family evidence is weaker. The remaining driver genes (MTOR, TP53, KDM5C, SETD2, and others) show no significant enrichment or depletion, and CDKN2A has no events in either group, so no effect is estimable. The exploratory non-driver genes show only nominal associations that do not survive global correction. Overall, the mutation data describe a driver-level phenotype centered on the VHL/PBRM1/BAP1 axis, with the caveat that only VHL is significant across the full tested-gene family.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior reports for this partition include structural diagnostics (weak between-set boundary in fused affinity, comparable internal cohesion, eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution), RNA pathway enrichment for both sets (K2_C0001 up in oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs; K2_C0002 the reciprocal), and confounder associations (tissue source site and CT acquisition factors significantly associated with membership). evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: The structural diagnostics describe the current two-set partition in the fused patient geometry. Both candidate sets are moderately sized and roughly balanced (55 and 48), and their mean within-set affinities are essentially identical (about 0.00932 for both), indicating comparable internal cohesion. The mean between-set affinity (about 0.00902) is only marginally lower than the within-set values, and the boundary silhouette is near zero (0.0003), so the current boundary between K2_C0001 and K2_C0002 is not sharply separated in this fused affinity representation. The union eigengap profile is dominated by the leading gap at the single-cluster resolution (candidate_k = 1, leading gap 0.476 versus subsequent gaps of 0.0006-0.002), so this screening calculation describes dominance of the single-cluster resolution and does not identify a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal; it does not provide feasible k>=2 set-level solutions and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Overall, the measurements indicate that the two current sets are internally cohesive to a similar degree and that their mutual boundary is relatively weak in fused affinity terms, while the internal screening results are dominated by the single-cluster resolution rather than by any feasible internal split.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior Evidence Reports for this partition include RNA pathway enrichment for both sets (K2_C0001 up in oxidative phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative programs; K2_C0002 the reciprocal), confounder associations (tissue source site and CT acquisition factors significantly associated with membership), and WXS mutation enrichment (a reciprocal VHL/PBRM1-versus-BAP1 driver axis). Those reports describe biological and technical characterization of the sets but do not speak to the fused patient geometry, so they neither confirm nor contradict the weak structural boundary reported here. The confounder associations are the most relevant tension: significant site and acquisition associations could contribute to the fused geometry in which the boundary is weak, but association is not proof of artifact, and the structural report cannot adjudicate that question. The RNA and WXS reports describe coherent set-level biology that is complementary to, rather than in conflict with, the geometric picture.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: This report addresses whether the current K2_C0001/K2_C0002 memberships, internal structures, and boundary are coherently represented across the four native patient geometries. The current-label alignment is weak in every single view: the boundary silhouette is near zero in CT (0.013) and small in WSI (0.050), RNA (0.079), and WXS (0.091), and in each modality the mean between-label distance exceeds the mean within-label distance only marginally. This means the current pair boundary is directionally present but not sharply expressed in any one modality's native distance geometry, and the tool performs no reclustering, so these values describe alignment of the existing labels rather than a re-derived partition.
